title: India's SEBI Launches Tokenized Bond Pilot with $107 Million in Issuance
dek: India's securities regulator deployed the Demat 2.0 pilot, issuing $107 million in tokenized corporate bonds settled via wholesale CBDC and smart contracts on a distributed ledger. The program marks a major sovereign regulator's first live deployment of tokenized securities at institutional scale.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: $107 million in tokenized corporate bonds issued through SEBI's Demat 2.0 pilot, settled using India's wholesale CBDC and distributed ledger technology.
bottom_line: The outcome to watch is whether the $107 million issuance sustains momentum into Q4 2026 or remains a one-time pilot exercise. The key test: does a second round of issuance occur, and do international regulators cite this model as precedent for their own institutional tokenization frameworks.
body: India's Securities and Exchange Board (SEBI) has deployed Demat 2.0, a live pilot program for tokenized corporate bonds, with $107 million in issuance already recorded. According to Cointelegraph's reporting, settlement occurs via wholesale CBDC and distributed ledger technology, with smart contracts automating the bond servicing and clearing process.

The pilot represents a sovereign regulator's first institutional-scale deployment of tokenized securities on a blockchain-based infrastructure. Rather than pilot-only testing on sandboxed networks, Demat 2.0 has moved to live issuance and settlement, using India's own wholesale CBDC as the settlement currency and distributed ledger technology as the rails.

Smart contracts handle settlement and service of the bonds on the DLT platform, according to Cointelegraph. The use of a nation's CBDC for settlement distinguishes this from prior tokenized-bond experiments in other jurisdictions, which have relied on traditional payment systems or cryptocurrency settlement layers.

The program name, Demat 2.0, signals an upgrade to India's existing Dematerialized Securities (Demat) account infrastructure, the decades-old system for holding shares and bonds in electronic form. The tokenization addition extends that infrastructure into blockchain-native asset issuance and clearing.
